task.goal: Build `wordfreq`, a small Node.js command-line tool that prints the N most frequent words in a text file, with tests and a README. Use only the Node.js standard library.
task.result:
Implemented `wordfreq` in `/workspace` using only the Node.js standard library.

- `wordfreq.js` provides the CLI (`node wordfreq.js <file> [N]`) and exports `topWords(text, n)`.
- `README.md` documents usage, output, tokenization, ordering, and tests.
- `wordfreq.test.js` exercises CLI output, Unicode/punctuation tokenization, ordering, limits, and error cases.

The CLI defaults to 10 results and requires a positive safe integer for N. Words are case-folded and consist of Unicode letters/numbers; punctuation, including apostrophes, separates tokens. Results are sorted by descending frequency, then alphabetically.

Validation: `node --test` passed all 6 tests; an additional `topWords` module API smoke test passed.

Interface proposal: usage `node wordfreq.js <file> [N]`, N defaults 10; output one `word<TAB>count` per line sorted descending count, then alphabetically for ties; tokenize case-insensitively on Unicode letters/numbers with apostrophes treated as separators.
